resources.string: Noise reduction, sharpening, tone and the frame merge
%s. Photo size. The 2× modes merge on a twice denser grid: more detail, but about four times slower.
%s. How the finished frame is scaled down to the chosen size: Lanczos is sharpest, Bilinear is fastest.
Short frames for the highlights, long ones for the shadows: when, how many, how they blend
How many frames to merge. Higher: less noise and more detail, but slower; lower: faster but noisier. They come from the ZSL buffer: a smaller buffer merges as many as it holds.
%s. An extra very dark frame recovers overexposed areas (lamps, sky). Auto: only when something is clipped.
%s. How many dark frames to take. More: less noise in the highlights, but a slightly longer capture.
%s. How the dark frames are checked for motion. Stricter: fewer dark hand silhouettes over lamps.
Highlight frames: skip on motion, % of mask
Motion allowed in the clipped area. Higher: highlight frames used more often, scraps possible; lower: less often.
Highlight frames: how many times shorter than N
How many times darker the dark frame is. Higher: saves brighter lamps but noisier; lower: the opposite.
Highlight frames: clipping threshold for Auto
For Auto: share of clipped pixels from which the dark frame is taken. Higher: less often; lower: more often.
Extra bright frames after the press: less noise in the shadows. Off: faster, no risk of blur.
%s. When a bright frame is dropped: Auto if it is blurred, Always only if something moved.
Shadow frames: drop on motion, % of the frame
For Always: motion allowed in a bright frame. Higher: the frame is used more often; lower: less often.
How many bright frames to take. Higher: cleaner shadows, longer capture, more memory; lower: the opposite.
How much brighter the bright frames are. Higher: cleaner shadows but noisier frames; lower: the opposite.
%s. Where the sensor noise data comes from: the camera itself or your own settings.
Noise correction for bright areas. Higher: smoother, ghosts possible; lower: sharper and noisier.
Noise correction for dark areas. Higher: smoother shadows, ghosts possible; lower: sharper and noisier.
How the frames are aligned and merged into one
%s. Which frame alignment module to use: the system one (vivo only) or the one bundled with the app.
%s. Fine per-area frame alignment: more detail on handheld shots, adds about 0.8 s.
How ghosts of moving objects are removed
Strictness to motion. Higher: fewer ghosts, more noise; lower: more frames merged, ghosts possible.
How much frame difference is put down to noise. Higher: more frames merged; lower: stricter to motion.
How far rejection spreads to nearby areas. Lower: wider (fewer ghosts); higher: narrower.
Weak rejection below this counts as noise and does not spread. Higher: less noise; lower: fewer ghosts.
Removes ghosts harder where parts of the frame move differently (hands, foliage). Needs per-area alignment.
How textured an area must be for the boost. Lower: the boost acts more often; higher: less often.
Motion spread from which the boost turns on. Lower: fewer ghosts; higher: less noise.
How the frames blend into pixels: sharpness versus noise
%s. The newer way of blending frames: more detail at night and handheld. Off: the previous kernel.
New kernel, Auto: SNR key limit
For Auto: up to which light level the new kernel is used. Higher: brighter scenes too; lower: only in the dark.
New kernel by day: hand shake from, px
For Auto by day: hand shake from which the new kernel is used. Lower: more often (noisier on a tripod).
Blend width of the frames. Higher: softer and cleaner; lower: sharper but noisier.
Noise scale for the SNR key
Older kernel only: how noisy the shot is assumed to be. Higher: softer and cleaner; lower: sharper, noisier.
Older kernel only: how much noise is not taken for edges. Higher: smoother flat areas; lower: sharper.
Base kernel widening at low coverage
Where few frames were accepted (motion), the main frame is softened. Higher: more often, cleaner but softer.
Removes the colour zipper on edges of moving objects. Higher: stronger; lower: weaker; 0: off.
Keeps colour from bleeding along thin lines when the colour zipper is removed.
Highest weight of a bright frame in the merge. Higher: cleaner shadows; lower: bright frames count less.
How much more bright frames count than normal ones. Higher: cleaner shadows; lower: closer to normal frames.
Blur of very bright shadow frames. Higher: less shadow noise but less detail; 1: off.
Merge for cameras that deliver the frame as a Quad or Tetra mosaic
For cameras whose frame arrives as a Quad 2×2 or Tetra 4×4 mosaic. Below: the merge method and its settings.
Mosaic frames to merge. Higher: less noise but slower; lower: faster but noisier.
Split only: sharpness on edges. Lower: sharper but grainier; higher: softer.
%s. How a mosaic is merged. Native: faster and more detailed; subframe split: the older way.
Radius of the area samples are taken from. Higher: less noise but slower; lower: faster but noisier.
Uses the whole square area around a sample: less noise in flat areas. Off: as with the split.
Blend width of the native merge. Lower: sharper but noisier; higher: softer and cleaner.
Edge sharpness of the native merge. Lower: sharper, below 0.5 edges get coloured; higher: softer.
Smoothing of flat areas in the native merge. Higher: less noise there; lower: grainier.
%s. Limits how narrow the blend may get: protects edges from jaggies and coloured fringes.
Green blend width. Higher: narrower, sharper but noisier; lower: wider and softer.
The same for red and blue. Higher: sharper, more false colour; lower: softer colour.
%s. Fills in red and blue where samples are scarce. Helps with few frames; otherwise it colours edges.
When the colour fill acts. Higher: more often; lower: less often. Works only with the fill on.
%s. How a Tetra 4×4 mosaic is merged. T1: more detail and faster; the others are older ways.
Weight of the dark frame in clipped areas. Higher: it shapes the highlights more; lower: less.
Blur of the dark frame in the highlights. Higher: softer highlights; below 0.7: colour jaggies on edges.
Highlight frames: highlight edge colour, σ px
Colour smoothing on highlight edges. Higher: smoother colour; lower: a dotted colour line; 0: off.
For Auto: minimum sharpness of a bright frame. Higher: blurred ones dropped more often; lower: less often.
For Auto: how many times brighter a bright frame may be. Higher: brighter ones allowed; lower: dropped sooner.
Overexposed areas and stray coloured dots
Removes the magenta fringe around lamps and overexposed areas. Off: the old handling.
Hot pixel threshold (coloured dots at night). Lower: removes more, may touch detail; 0: off.
The same for random outliers of the main frame. Lower: removes more; higher: fewer; 0: off.
Hot pixels: only at SNR key ≤
Up to which light level outliers are searched. Higher: brighter scenes too; lower: only at night.
Checks the dark frame more strictly and skips it if it would spoil the photo. Off: the older checks.
Matching colour and brightness of bright frames to the main one
%s. Matches colour and brightness of bright frames to the main one before merging, so colours do not shift.
How noise is removed after the merge
All SHDR denoisers. Off: only the frame merge is left, so the shot is grainier but more detailed.
%s. Which denoiser cleans the shot after the merge. NLM is the older one with its own two strengths.
Removes single bright and dark dots. May erase small distant objects on sky or water.
Highlight frames: denoise boost limit in highlights
How much harder areas made from few frames are cleaned (lamps, motion). Higher: cleaner; lower: more detail.
NLM only: luma denoise strength. Higher: smoother; lower: more grain and detail; 0: off.
NLM only: colour denoise strength. Higher: fewer colour blotches; lower: more accurate colour; 0: off.
How the camera estimates the noise of the shot
Manual frame cleanliness (SNR), 0: auto. Higher: uses the bright-scene settings; lower: the night ones.
Correction of the auto SNR. Higher: the shot is treated as brighter and cleaner; lower: darker and noisier.
Noise model correction for mid and bright tones. Higher: stronger smoothing; lower: more detail.
Noise model correction for the shadows. Higher: smoother shadows; lower: more detail and grain in shadows.
%s. Clean harder where few frames were merged (lamps, motion), or evenly over the whole frame.
Overall strength multipliers of the multiscale denoiser
Overall luma denoise strength. Higher: smoother; lower: more grain and detail; 0: off.
Luma denoise strength at night, in dim and in normal light. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail.
Luma denoise strength at dusk and in bright light. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail.
Overall colour denoise strength. Higher: fewer colour blotches; lower: more accurate colour; 0: off.
How much fine grain is put back after denoising. Higher: sharper and grainier; lower: smoother.
Denoiser tweaks; same as ArkCam by default
Limit of the grain put back, matters at night. 1: never more grain than the shot had (default); above 1 the grain is amplified; 0: none.
Cleaning of large luma blotches. Higher: fewer blotches but washed-out texture; 0: texture is left alone.
Minimum colour denoise strength in any light. Higher: smoother colour even in daylight; 0: no minimum.
2× grid only: share of fine colour kept. Higher: more colour detail and colour noise; lower: cleaner colour.
Fade colour in the darkest areas
Removes the colour tint in near-black areas: the darkest pixels become neutral.
Luma denoise values for each light level
Night point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Night: luma denoise strength, 5 numbers fine to coarse grain. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail.
Night: grain put back, 5 numbers fine to coarse. Higher: sharper, grainier; lower: smoother.
Night: luma smoothing reach, 5 numbers 0–1. Higher: smoother but softer edges; lower: crisper edges.
Dusk point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Dusk: luma denoise strength, 5 numbers fine to coarse grain. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail.
Dusk: grain put back, 5 numbers fine to coarse. Higher: sharper, grainier; lower: smoother.
Dusk: luma smoothing reach, 5 numbers 0–1. Higher: smoother but softer edges; lower: crisper edges.
Dim light point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Dim light: luma denoise strength, 5 numbers fine to coarse grain. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail.
Dim light: grain put back, 5 numbers fine to coarse. Higher: sharper, grainier; lower: smoother.
Dim light: luma smoothing reach, 5 numbers 0–1. Higher: smoother but softer edges; lower: crisper edges.
Normal light point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Normal light: luma denoise strength, 5 numbers fine to coarse grain. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail.
Normal light: grain put back, 5 numbers fine to coarse. Higher: sharper, grainier; lower: smoother.
Normal light: luma smoothing reach, 5 numbers 0–1. Higher: smoother but softer edges; lower: crisper edges.
Bright light point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Bright light: luma denoise strength, 5 numbers fine to coarse grain. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail.
Bright light: grain put back, 5 numbers fine to coarse. Higher: sharper, grainier; lower: smoother.
Bright light: luma smoothing reach, 5 numbers 0–1. Higher: smoother but softer edges; lower: crisper edges.
Colour denoise values for each light level
Deep night point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Deep night: colour smoothing reach, 5 integers 0–16. Higher: smoother but colour bleeds; lower: crisper.
Night point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Night: colour smoothing reach, 5 integers 0–16. Higher: smoother but colour bleeds; lower: crisper.
Dusk point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Dusk: colour smoothing reach, 5 integers 0–16. Higher: smoother but colour bleeds; lower: crisper.
Dim light point: the SNR where it applies. Higher: used on brighter shots; lower: on darker ones.
Dim light: colour smoothing reach, 5 integers 0–16. Higher: smoother but colour bleeds; lower: crisper.
The only sharpening of the photo: ArkCam sharpening of brightness before the tone. Defaults as ArkCam; the rows below weaken or strengthen it.
How much ARK fine detail goes into the photo. Higher: sharper, crisper; lower: softer; 0: no detail.
%s. Brightness ARK sharpening is computed on. After exposure: weaker on strong edges in dark scenes.
Scale of ARK sharpening radii; 0: auto by photo size. Higher: coarser sharpening; lower: finer.
ARK unsharp mask radius. Higher: thicker outlines, more halos; lower: finer; 0: off.
ARK unsharp mask noise threshold. Higher: weak detail and noise not boosted; lower: sharper, noisier.
Size of the lifted detail. Higher: larger detail is lifted; lower: only the finest; 0: off.
Lift of fine detail, edges barely touched. Higher: sharper, noisier; lower: softer; 0: off.
Brightness step treated as an edge and not lifted. Higher: edges get lifted too; lower: only fine detail.
ARK local contrast radius. Higher: works on larger structures; lower: on smaller; 0: off.
Local contrast threshold. Higher: stronger edges are boosted too; lower: only faint texture.
ARK local contrast strength. Higher: more depth and punch; lower: flatter; below 0: smooths.
Artificial film grain, strongest in midtones. Higher: more visible grain; 0: no grain.
Three RL sharpness recovery stages and halo suppression.
RL halo suppression, %. Higher: fewer edge fringes; lower: crisper, with fringes.
RL overshoot allowance on weak edges. Higher: crisper texture, risk of fringes; lower: stricter.
Contrast from which RL fades on strong edges. Higher: crisper edges, more halos; lower: softer.
%s. Shape of the blur RL stage 1 corrects.
Size of the blur corrected. Higher: fixes heavier blur, risk of halos; lower: finer; 0: stage off.
%s. Blur shape that stage 2 removes (defocus, medium details).
Size of the blur that stage 2 removes. Higher: works on larger details; 0: stage off.
%s. Blur shape that stage 3 removes (fine texture).
Blur size for stage 3, px. Higher: coarser sharpening; lower: finer; 0: stage off.
Weakens sharpening in shadows so noise is not boosted. Higher: softer, cleaner shadows; 0: no protection.
Weakens sharpening in bright areas. Higher: softer highlights without halos; lower: sharper.
Limits halos on strong edges. Higher: fewer halos; lower: crisper edges, but with halos.
Exposure, Smart HDR, layer weights and tone curves of ARK.
%s. Which part of the frame sets the exposure.
Target brightness of the photo. Higher: brighter; lower: darker.
How much a bright scene may be darkened. Lower: bright scenes darker; higher: brighter.
How much a dark scene may be brightened. Higher: brighter and noisier; lower: darker.
How much clipping the exposure allows. Higher: brighter, more clipped highlights; lower: darker.
Strength of auto exposure. Above 1: stronger brightness correction; below 1: weaker, closer to the original.
Gain limit set by sensor noise. Higher: brighter, noisier night shots; lower: darker, cleaner.
Input brightness scale, EV. Keep 0 for SHDR. Higher: brighter; lower: darker; AE partly evens it out.
Level where Smart HDR starts to darken highlights. Higher: brighter highlights; lower: more compressed.
Shadow lift threshold of Smart HDR. Lower: shadows lifted more; higher: less.
When a scene counts as flat and gets extra contrast. Higher: more often; lower: less often.
Multiplier of highlight compression. Higher: darker, more detailed highlights; lower: brighter; 0: none.
Extra contrast for flat scenes. Higher: flat scenes get more contrast; 0: none.
How much Smart HDR lifts shadows. Higher: brighter shadows; lower: darker.
How much Smart HDR darkens highlights. Higher: darker, more detailed highlights; lower: brighter.
Weight of the first brightened layer. Higher: brighter shadows and midtones; lower: darker.
Weight of the dark layer for highlights. Higher: darker, more detailed highlights; lower: brighter.
Weight of the normal exposure layer. Higher: closer to the original; lower: stronger HDR effect.
Weight of the brightest layer for shadows. Higher: lighter deep shadows; lower: darker.
Output gamma. Higher: lighter midtones and shadows, flatter; lower: darker, more contrast.
Deepens the darkest tones. Higher: deeper blacks; lower: lighter shadows; 0: off.
AgX by default; ACES, Uchimura or your own curve instead.
%s. Preset look of the AgX curve; Custom uses the settings below.
Contrast of the AgX curve (Custom look). Higher: more contrast; lower: softer, flatter.
OPPO Find X7 Ultra only: saturation with the OPPO colour matrix. Higher: richer colours; lower: paler.
Softness of the deepest shadows in the ACES curve. Higher: softer fade to black; lower: harder.
Boost of fine detail. Higher: crisper; below 0: softer.
Contrast of midtones. Higher: more contrast; lower: softer.
Layer brightness the fusion prefers. Higher: brighter picture; lower: darker.
How smoothly layers mix. Higher: softer, more natural; lower: stronger HDR effect.
Zone size of the fusion map, px. Higher: tone follows large areas; lower: follows small details.
Smoothing of the fusion map. Higher: smoother, more global; lower: more precise at edges.
Adds SCAMERA local contrast after the ARK tone: textures look stronger.
Colour recovery of clipped highlights, %. Higher: stronger; lower: weaker; 0: off.
Highlights: trust threshold for surrounding colour
How coloured the light around a clip may be. Higher: the clip takes its colour; lower: stays whiter.
Removes colour fringes at clipped highlights. Higher: stronger; lower: weaker; 0: off.
Smooths the coloured dotted line on clipped edges. Higher: stronger; lower: weaker; 0: off.
Denoise of the brightest areas (the short highlight frame). Higher: cleaner; lower: more detail; 0: off.
Path to white for bright coloured light
Blown light rises smoothly to pure white, a coloured light to its own colour at full brightness. Higher: the roll-off starts earlier and is softer; 0: off (the tone curve alone).
Bright coloured light (LED, neon) turns white. Higher: whitens sooner; lower: keeps colour; 0: off.
Removes the coloured line on the dark side of contrasty edges. Higher: stronger; 0: off.
Suppresses noise on flat areas. Higher: cleaner, but fine texture is lost; 0: off.
Removes colour noise in strongly lifted shadows. Higher: cleaner, but paler shadows; 0: off.
Colour vibrance: overall, sky and greenery.
Vibrance of muted colours; vivid ones are left alone. Higher: richer; lower: paler.
Vibrance of blue sky. Higher: deeper sky; lower: paler.
Vibrance of greenery. Higher: richer greens; lower: paler.
System encoder: about twice as fast, but the file is a bit larger and fine colour detail is coarser.
Logs the time of every shot stage to a file to find what is slow. Merging is slower; the photo is the same.
Saves the intermediate stages of a shot into a ZIP for analysis. Slows processing and takes space.
The scam_dev.txt file changes these settings without the menu, with key value lines.
Network for Tetra 4×4: strength, noise, ISO
Works on the telephoto lens in 4× ISZ mode, Tetra 4×4. Settings apply to the next shot. For the old result: x2, multipliers 1, auto by ISO off, texture 0.
The CPU, GPU and NPU work at the same time, which is faster. Always on; info only.
x1 is an experimental model: it had colour errors in tests. The chosen model and profile are checked before shooting. Both options use six frames.
How noisy the network assumes the frame is, 1 is original. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail and noise.
Bright-area noise for the network, 1 is original. Higher: smoother bright areas; lower: more detail.
Shadow noise for the network, 1 is original. Higher: smoother shadows; lower: more detail and noise.
Network share in luma. Higher: smoother and cleaner; lower: more original texture and noise.
Network share in colour. Higher: less colour noise; lower: more colour noise.
Brings back texture on detail by lowering the network share. Higher: more texture, but grain may return.
The network share follows ISO between the values below. The manual Luma and Chroma are then not used.
Network share in luma at ISO 100 and below. Higher: smoother; lower: more texture and noise.
Network share in colour at ISO 100 and below. Higher: less colour noise; lower: more.
Network share in luma at ISO 3200 and above. Higher: smoother; lower: more texture and noise.
Network share in colour at ISO 3200 and above. Higher: less colour noise; lower: more.
Network for Quad 2×2: strength, noise, ISO
Works in 2× ISZ mode (HP9 telephoto or IMX06C main/wide), Quad 2×2 mosaic. Luma and chroma blend the network output with the reconstruction of the first RAW.
How noisy the network assumes the frame is, 1 is original. Higher: smoother; lower: more detail and noise.
Bright-area noise for the network, 1 is original. Higher: smoother bright areas; lower: more detail.
Shadow noise for the network, 1 is original. Higher: smoother shadows; lower: more detail and noise.
Network share in luma. Higher: smoother and cleaner; lower: more original texture and noise.
Network share in colour. Higher: less colour noise; lower: more colour noise.
The network share follows ISO between the values below. The manual Luma and Chroma are then not used.
Network share in luma at ISO 100 and below. Higher: smoother; lower: more texture and noise.
Network share in colour at ISO 100 and below. Higher: less colour noise; lower: more.
Network share in luma at ISO 3200 and above. Higher: smoother; lower: more texture and noise.
Network share in colour at ISO 3200 and above. Higher: less colour noise; lower: more.
Colour block size of the mosaic when the module does not report it: 2×2 Quad or 4×4 Tetra.
DCP colour matrices of the modules
Colour matrix of the module: the camera one or an imported DCP. Changes how colours look.
ZSL buffer, lamp flicker, DNG, RAW levels, noise model
DNG is compressed losslessly: about 40 percent smaller, a bit slower to save. Not every app reads it.
%s. Evens out the brightness of the frame corners. Do not apply: if the camera already fixed the RAW.
If the camera reports black too high, black is taken from the frame itself. Removes green shadows.
%s. How the camera delivers RAW. Auto: 16-bit if offered, otherwise RAW10 or RAW12.
Dynamic black and white levels, front camera mirroring
Sensor noise profile, import and export
The chosen profile replaces the camera noise in the SHDR denoise, the DNG and merges set to From settings.
Sounds, grid, focus, faces, HUD, horizon and theme
A click when shooting. Only in normal ringer mode; where the law requires it, it always plays.
Audible self-timer countdown. Only in normal ringer mode.
Colour of highlights, switches and camera buttons.
Photo format and quality, colour, Ultra HDR, 16:9, file name, watermark, settings backup
JPEG compression. Higher: larger, more detailed file; lower: smaller file, fine detail lost.
Line text, icon, size and opacity
Caption height in percent of the photo height. Higher: bigger caption; lower: smaller.
Caption opacity. 100: solid; lower: more see-through.
The config moves to another phone: lens profiles are matched by focal length.
Camera modules, their profiles and zoom, sensor settings
Telephoto: 3.2–4.3x optical, then crop, from 6.45x in-sensor zoom. Off: zoom without these modes.
Root, package spoofing, diagnostics, log, developer options, about
Optional. Adds a fallback way to start the processing if the usual one fails.
Logs and checks with a report
Check loading the neural remosaic onto the neural accelerator and copy the report.
The camera sees another app name and unlocks hidden modules
Show the camera another app name. Off: SCAMERA as it is. Applies when the camera next opens.
OPPO / OnePlus: hidden cameras; generic: in-app spoof; BinderHook: experimental. Empty: own package.
Which format photos are saved in. JPEG opens everywhere; HEIC, WebP and AVIF are smaller, not universal.
HEIC compression. Higher: larger, more detailed file; lower: smaller file, fine detail lost.
10 bits per colour instead of 8: smooth sky gradients without banding. Needs Android 13+.
WebP compression. Higher: larger, more detailed file; lower: smaller file, fine detail lost.
Exact pixels: the file is several times larger and slower to save. Quality is ignored.
AVIF compression. Higher: larger, more detailed file; lower: smaller file, fine detail lost.
Exact pixels: the file is about 6 times larger and slower to save.
Bits per colour. 10: smooth gradients, 12: room for editing, 8: like JPEG.
Colour resolution. 4:4:4: sharp coloured edges; 4:2:0: smaller file, softer edges.
AVIF saving speed. Slower: slightly better detail; faster: slightly worse.
sRGB looks the same everywhere. Display P3: richer colours on P3 screens; flatter where P3 is ignored.
Adds an HDR gain map, as Ultra HDR in JPEG: HDR screens show brighter highlights, other screens the normal photo.
A JPEG copy next to the HEIC / WebP / AVIF for apps that cannot open them.
Finds faces, frames them and aims focus and exposure at them. Manual focus and a tap win.
How to start tracking: focus and exposure follow the chosen subject across the frame.
How much of the look of the LUT goes into the photo: 0 — none, 100 — all of it.
A tap puts the focus ring and the exposure square around it; drag each where you need it. Tap the ring to return to auto, tap the square to bring it back to the ring.
Merges at 2× only in good light and if frames add detail. Otherwise 1× and upscaling: faster, no grid pattern
ARK unsharp mask strength. Higher: sharper; lower: softer; 0: off.
Strength of sharpening stage 1 (lens diffraction). Higher: sharper; lower: softer; 0: off.
Passes of stage 1. Higher: stronger and slower, halos possible; lower: weaker; 0: off.
Strength of stage 2 (medium details). Higher: sharper; lower: softer; 0: off.
Passes of stage 2. Higher: stronger and slower, halos possible; lower: weaker; 0: off.
Strength of stage 3 (fine texture). Higher: sharper; lower: softer; 0: off.
Passes of stage 3. Higher: stronger and slower, halos possible; lower: weaker; 0: off.
Roll-off into white (Custom look). Higher: highlights stay bright longer, harder roll-off; lower: softer.
Roll-off into black (Custom look). Higher: denser, darker shadows; lower: softer, lighter shadows.
Lower end of the AgX range (Custom look). Lower: more shadow detail, flatter; higher: darker shadows.
Highlight headroom of AgX (Custom look). Higher: less clipping, flatter; lower: highlights hit white sooner.
Saturation after AgX (Custom look). Higher: richer colours; lower: paler; 0: black and white.
Exposure before the AgX curve (Custom look). Higher: brighter; lower: darker.
Show the camera icon in the caption.
Load settings from a saved file.
Return all settings to default. The app restarts.
How many times rejection is boosted. Higher: fewer ghosts but more noise; lower: the opposite.
Deep night: colour denoise strength, 5 numbers small to large blotches. Higher: cleaner; lower: truer colour.
Night: colour denoise strength, 5 numbers small to large blotches. Higher: cleaner; lower: truer colour.
Dusk: colour denoise strength, 5 numbers small to large blotches. Higher: cleaner; lower: truer colour.
Dim light: colour denoise strength, 5 numbers small to large blotches. Higher: cleaner; lower: truer colour.
Which network builds the Tetra frame. x2 is the main one; x1 is experimental and may give colour errors.
Vertical offset of the block grid. A wrong value gives a colour grid; the neural mode needs 0.
Save, restore or reset the settings
ISZ modules on the Snapdragon 8 Elite: the NPU network merges the N frames
ISZ modules with a Quad / Tetra mosaic: the vivo network on the NPU merges the N frames first, then SHDR. If it fails, the usual mosaic merge.
What the merge wrote for the last shot: for looking into a failed or odd photo
Every photo warmer or cooler on top of the auto white balance. Higher: warmer; lower: cooler; 0: as measured.
Green or magenta on top of the auto white balance. Higher: more magenta; lower: greener; 0: as measured.
Under tungsten lamps and at sunset part of the warmth stays instead of being neutralised (from 5000 K, fully at 2700 K). 0: the light is fully neutralised.
In shade and overcast part of the blue stays (from 7000 K, fully at 12000 K). 0: the light is fully neutralised.
Dull colours in the shadows richer or calmer. Higher: richer; lower: calmer, more neutral shadows; 0: off.
Dull colours in the bright areas richer or calmer. Higher: richer; lower: calmer; 0: off.
Faces keep their colour when vibrance, the AgX saturation, the colour mixer or the grading add colour. Higher: stronger protection; 0: off.
Skin redder or more golden; other colours stay as they are. Higher: more golden; lower: redder; 0: as is.
Evens out blotchy redness by drawing the hues of skin together. Higher: more even; 0: off.
Hue, saturation and lightness of 8 colours
Turns this colour towards its neighbours on the colour wheel. 0: as is.
Higher: lighter; lower: darker; 0: as is.
Tint the shadows, mid-tones and highlights
Colour of the tint on the colour wheel: 0 red, 60 yellow, 120 green, 180 cyan, 240 blue, 300 magenta.
How strong the tint is. 0: off.
Where the shadows end and the highlights begin. Higher: more of the picture counts as highlights; lower: as shadows.
How smoothly the zones run into each other.
%s. Black and white with the filter of black-and-white film: yellow darkens the sky a little, orange and red more, green lightens foliage, blue lightens the sky.
Neon, LED and other very saturated colours keep their hue instead of clipping. Higher: stronger; 0: off.
%s. Whether the tone curve may shift hues (bright blues turning purple, oranges turning yellow). Full: no shift; blues only: only the blues are held; off: as the curve does.
Hue and saturation of the camera\'s red, green and blue
Turns this primary of the camera, and every colour made of it, round the colour wheel. 0: as the camera renders it.
Higher: this primary richer; lower: duller; 0: as the camera renders it. White stays white.
The ACES curve (ArkCam): more contrast, highlights roll off softly. Turns the other curves off.
Multiplies the linear signal before the curve: higher is brighter.
Top of the curve: higher gives brighter highlights and more contrast.
Bottom of the curve: higher gives softer mid-tones and darker highlights.
